children: Mumbai: Adani Group plans to invest an aggregate of Rs 2.20 lakh crore in the current fiscal ended March 2027, up from Rs 1.56 lakh crore last fiscal group Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of the Adani Group is Jugeshinder Singh said. The group has planned market borrowings of Rs 1.3 lakh crore to Rs 1.4 lakh crore each broadly for the current and next fiscal year, Singh said.

"We can invest close to Rs 2.20 lakh crore which is largely constrained by the fact that (we cannot) complete that much on the ground, we don't have the capability. In fact the country as a whole will take time to build that ecosystem...the health systems, the education systems, the core manufacturing, cold storage systems. We need to build out the core infra which we are not building at fast enough speed that the country needs," Singh said.
The group plans to borrow Rs 1.3 lakh crore to Rs 1.4 lakh crore borrowing in the next fiscal year ended March 2028 which is broadly the same as they borrowed in the current fiscal year, Singh said.

Singh said the group will be ready to demerge its airports business in the next fiscal year after which the board will decide when to go for an IPO. Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL), owns, operates, or holds majority stakes in eight airports across the country.

Singh said the airports business is now ready to fund its own investment plan and the group wants its non aero revenue which is money earned through commercial or non flight activities to be about 65% of total revenues before it can be demerged.

"The non-aero income broadly where we want to see in terms of percentage. So it's going in the right direction. As as those business cases solidify more over the next six months to nine months, with non-aero on average somewhere between 60-65%, then yes (we can demerge)," Singh said adding its roughly just around 60% now.

Singh said the company will continue to borrow from the domestic and overseas markets with both Adani Power and Adani Enterprises likely to tap the domestic market for a public issue of rupee bonds next fiscal.
Another group company Adani Ports also will likely tap the overseas market for a 20 year dollar bond next fiscal year, Singh said.

"It will mostly be for refinance though they do have enough cash to just retire the debt. There is a $600 million maturity coming too so we will replace some (debt) with. (But) we want to issue some long dated paper (too)," Singh said.
The group expects gross debt on its books to be broadly between 3 to 3.2 times EBITDA (earnings before interest tax depreciation and amortisation) which is about Rs 3.9 lakh crore.
The Adani Group aims to increase the percentage of domestic borrowings to close to 80% from 56% currently.
"Ultimately infra is domestic and we have to create wealth for domestic participants so they must we should create opportunities for them to participate," Singh said.

For its data centre business Singh said has bank lines of $3 billion out of which $900 million has been raised and $10 billion is likely to be raised in the next four years.<meta content="cms.article3" name="cmsei-article3"/> For Reprint Rights: timescontent.com

title: Adani Group plans capex increase, aims higher domestic borrowings
